model_annotation: Figure 2 presents two bar charts comparing inference times (in seconds) for baseline Llama models and their distilled counterparts—pure Mamba and hybrid MambaInLlama—at the 1B and 3B parameter scales, respectively. In (a), for 1B models, the x-axis represents batch size (linear scale, values: 1, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 300), while the y-axis shows inference time (linear scale, 0 to 10 seconds). Llama-1B (blue) exhibits increasing inference time with batch size, from ~1.6s at batch 1 to ~9.5s at batch 300. Llama-1B (orange) shows similar trends but slightly lower times (e.g., ~1.3s at batch 1, ~8.7s at batch 300). MambaInLlama-1B (red) consistently outperforms both, with inference times ranging from ~1.1s at batch 1 to ~4.7s at batch 300. In (b), for 3B models, the x-axis again represents batch size (linear scale, values: 1, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512), and the y-axis shows inference time (linear scale, 0 to 30 seconds). Llama-3B (blue) increases from ~2.6s to ~28s. Llama-3B (orange) ranges from ~2.6s to ~24.7s. MambaInLlama-3B (red) remains fastest, from ~2.3s at batch 1 to ~10s at batch 512. The caption notes that for 512 completions using a batch size of 512, the MambaInLlama-3B model achieves a 5.1x speedup over Llama-3B, which would take 11.6s.
